luma-evt-c8bSoEY0K3wEXlL.summaryLead: A full-day crypto education camp at Paris La Défense, organized by Nairod Invest and supported by CryptoMondays Paris, covering everything from blockchain basics to hands-on trading workshops.

sections.heading: What This Day Is About
content: CryptoMondays X Nairod Invest Day is a one-day intensive running from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM on Friday, August 28, 2026, at 25 Quai du Président Paul Doumer in Courbevoie — right at Paris La Défense, accessible via Métro 1, Esplanade de la Défense. The event is organized by Nairod Invest, an organization incubated by CCI Paris, and CryptoMondays Paris is backing it with a featured speaker session.

The format is built around a progression from absolute basics to practical skill-building. The morning starts with understanding blockchain, Bitcoin, and the broader crypto ecosystem — exchanges, wallets, DeFi protocols, and stablecoins. By the afternoon, attendees move into security practices, investment strategies, risk management, and live market analysis. The idea is that you walk in knowing nothing and walk out with a working understanding of how to buy, store, and evaluate a crypto asset.

sections.heading: The Agenda in Detail
content: The program covers a wide spread of topics across the day. Early sessions focus on foundational knowledge: what blockchain technology is, how Bitcoin fits into the picture, and what the various corners of the crypto ecosystem actually do. The middle of the day shifts toward security — protecting your assets, recognizing scams, and understanding the real risks involved in holding digital currencies.

The afternoon gets more hands-on. There are workshops on using an exchange platform and setting up a wallet, plus a session on reading and interpreting crypto market data. The final block walks through building your own investment strategy simulation, where participants work through real scenarios before putting money on the line. A live Q&A wraps things up, giving the group a chance to surface remaining questions. Ksenia Drobyshevskaya from CryptoMondays Paris joins for a special interview session during the day.

sections.heading: Who Should Show Up
content: This event explicitly targets two audiences: people who have never touched crypto and people who already hold positions but want to refine their approach. That breadth is unusual for a crypto meetup — most events either assume baseline knowledge or cater exclusively to veterans. Nairod Invest seems to have designed this day so a complete beginner can follow along without feeling lost, while an experienced holder still gets value from the strategy and analysis workshops.

Places are limited and reservation is required, so registering early through the Luma page is important. The event runs on Friday, which means a full workday commitment, but the payoff is a structured educational experience rather than a casual evening talk. If you have been curious about crypto but unsure where to start, or if you have been trading informally and want to build a more disciplined framework, this is a solid use of a day.

sections.heading: Practical Details Worth Knowing
content: The venue is at Paris La Défense, one of Europe's largest business districts, so there are plenty of dining and transport options nearby. Doors open at 9:00 AM with the program officially starting at 9:30 AM, so arriving early gives you time to settle in. The event runs until 6:00 PM, making it a genuine full-day commitment.

CryptoMondays Paris is the presenting organizer, and the event carries the network's community-driven ethos — accessible, educational, and focused on real participation rather than passive listening. The collaboration with Nairod Invest and CCI Paris adds institutional weight, suggesting the content has been vetted beyond what a typical meetup organizer might produce. If you are in the Paris area and want a structured introduction to crypto investing, this is one of the better options on the calendar for late August.

luma-host-evt-dSVTRTCeQZKE3Ec.summaryLead: A free weekly co-working and learning session in downtown Toronto, hosted by Superteam Canada, where Solana builders gather every Friday to work, connect, and share knowledge.

sections.heading: What Happens at VibeStation
content: Toronto Solana VibeStation runs every Friday from 9:30 AM to 6:00 PM in downtown Toronto. It is organized by Superteam Canada, the community arm focused on growing the Solana ecosystem across the country. The format is straightforward: show up, grab a desk or couch or private room, and spend the day building alongside other people working in web3.

The event is not a typical sit-and-listen meetup. It is designed as an active co-working space with educational programming layered in. Expect workshops, panels, and keynotes covering Solana, DeFi, DAOs, NFTs, and related topics. The content rotates based on what partners and community members bring to the table each week, so the experience shifts depending on when you show up.

sections.heading: The Solana Angle
content: Superteam Canada is specifically focused on growing the Solana ecosystem, so the programming leans toward Solana-native tools, protocols, and projects. If you are building on Solana or thinking about it, this is a place to get direct support from people who know the stack. The event description mentions receiving support and advice from Solana experts, plus open mics and demo days where you can showcase your work.

The community aspect is a big part of the draw. You are not just working alone in a room with other people — the format encourages collaboration, finding team members, and networking with builders who might be working on complementary projects. For someone solo-building a Solana project, showing up consistently to a weekly session like this can be the difference between grinding in isolation and finding the collaborators who help you ship.

sections.heading: Logistics and Registration
content: Attendance is free, but registration through the Luma page is required because the venue has limited capacity. The exact address is revealed after you register, which is a common pattern for Superteam events — it keeps the room from being overrun by walk-ins while maintaining a sense of exclusivity for committed attendees. The venue is described as a downtown co-working space equipped with free drinks and snacks.

There are two ticket tiers: a Standard option and a Members-Only option for Superteam members. If you are not yet a member, the Standard ticket gets you in the door. For ongoing updates, the Solana Canada Telegram group (https://t.me/+Dm3WujI--Go1ZjQ0/SuperteamCAN) is the central communication channel. Since this is a weekly recurring event, you can drop in on a Friday that works for your schedule rather than committing to a single date.

sections.heading: Why This Model Works
content: The VibeStation concept solves a real problem in the web3 space: most crypto events are either too educational (panels with no room to apply what you learn) or too social (drinks and networking with no substance). This format splits the difference by giving you a full day of productive workspace with structured learning woven in. You can spend the morning at a workshop and the afternoon heads-down on your own project, all within the same community environment.

For Toronto's growing web3 scene, having a reliable weekly gathering point matters. It creates consistency — you know where to be every Friday — and that consistency builds the kind of community where real collaborations happen. Whether you are a developer, designer, project lead, or just someone exploring the Solana ecosystem, the low barrier to entry and high ceiling on what you can get out of it make this worth putting on your calendar.

Workshops, panels, and keynotes from partners cover Solana, DeFi, DAOs, NFTs, and adjacent topics. The programming changes week to week based on who is presenting, which means each Friday has a slightly different flavor.

sections.heading: Building in Montréal's Web3 Scene
content: Montréal has a distinct tech culture — strong on engineering talent, multilingual by nature, and increasingly active in the blockchain space. Superteam Canada's decision to run a dedicated VibeStation here reflects the city's growing relevance in the Canadian web3 ecosystem. For builders based in Montréal, this is a chance to connect with the Solana community without traveling to Toronto.

The event description highlights hands-on experience: working on your project, finding team members, or joining an existing team. That practical focus matters. Web3 is full of people talking about building things — this space is designed for people who are actually doing it. Demo days and open mics give participants a platform to share what they have been working on, which creates accountability and visibility for ongoing projects.

sections.heading: Registration and Access
content: Like the other VibeStation events, attendance is free but registration through Luma is required due to limited venue capacity. Two ticket tiers exist: Standard for general attendees and Members-Only for Superteam members. The exact address is disclosed after registration, keeping the space manageable and focused on committed participants.

The venue is described as a comfortable downtown Montréal location with free drinks and snacks provided. The event runs five hours — 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM — which is shorter than the Toronto and Vancouver editions by about an hour. For ongoing coordination, the Solana Canada Telegram group serves as the primary communication channel. Since this repeats every Friday, you can pick the week that fits your schedule and register in advance to lock in a spot.

sections.heading: What Makes This Worth Your Friday
content: The value proposition of VibeStation is simple: instead of spending Friday working from your apartment or a coffee shop, you spend it in a room full of people who are building in the same space you are. The educational content adds a learning layer, but the real draw is the community density. When you are surrounded by other builders, conversations happen naturally, and those conversations often lead to collaborations that would never emerge from a screen.

For Montréal's web3 community specifically, having a reliable weekly gathering point creates the kind of infrastructure that lets a local scene mature. Newcomers get a low-pressure entry point, experienced builders get a consistent co-working environment, and the whole group benefits from the cross-pollination that happens when people show up regularly. If you are in Montréal and building on or interested in Solana, this is a straightforward way to plug into the ecosystem.

content: Getting face time with a VP of Product from a major blockchain foundation is not something that happens at a typical web3 meetup. Vibhu's role puts him at the center of how Solana's product direction evolves, so the fireside chat is a chance to hear directly about what the foundation is prioritizing, what product challenges they are wrestling with, and where they see opportunities for builders.

For someone building on Solana who has specific questions about product-market fit, ecosystem support, or technical direction, that kind of access is rare and valuable. sections.heading: Who Gets In

The exclusivity is by design — a smaller group creates better conversations and makes the networking portion genuinely useful rather than a crowded room where you struggle to find anyone to talk to.

For people who are not yet Superteam UK members, this event is a good reason to look into joining the community. Superteam runs a global network of Solana-focused communities, and membership gives you access to events like this one, plus the broader ecosystem of builders, mentors, and resources. The London chapter has been one of the more active European chapters, and events at Somerset House carry a certain weight that reflects the community's standing.

sections.heading: The Somerset House Setting
content: Somerset House is one of London's most recognized cultural venues, sitting on the South Bank of the Thames. Hosting a web3 community event there signals something about the Superteam UK community's positioning — this is not a meetup crammed into a co-working space's overflow room. The office setting keeps things professional while the fireside format and food keep things social.

The evening runs for three hours total, which is long enough to have meaningful conversations without burning out. Arriving at 6:00 PM gives you time to settle in before the fireside chat, and the open-ended structure from 7:00 PM onward means you can leave when you want or stay as long as the conversations are productive. If you are in the Superteam UK community and have not attended a member evening before, this one — with two Solana Foundation VPs in the room — is a strong first one to choose.

mu-314107814.summaryLead: A monthly online strategy discussion hosted by the Kansas City Business Strategy Group, examining why successful leaders sometimes limit their own growth by thinking too small about what their businesses can become.

sections.heading: The Core Question
content: Are You Thinking Too Small? That is the Question! is a one-hour online session happening Tuesday, September 1, 2026, at 11:30 AM CT. It is hosted by David B. through The International Business Strategy Group, a Kansas City-based Meetup community that meets on the first Tuesday of every month via Zoom. The event tackles a specific problem: why successful leaders often become prisoners of their own success.

The discussion frames this as a pattern rather than an individual failing. When your business is working well, there is a natural tendency to assume that what works today will work tomorrow. The event challenges that assumption by exploring why comfortable beliefs about your current business can quietly destroy valuation over time. It is a strategic conversation, not a tactical one — the focus is on mindset and direction, not on specific tools or frameworks.

sections.heading: How the Group Works
content: The Kansas City Business Strategy Group has a distinctive format. Once a month, members share insights on driving growth and value in their business enterprises. The group is described as diverse and dynamic, drawing from different industries and business stages. Each meeting features a topic that ranges from business planning to personal strategies, and the goal is for every participant to identify information and ideas they can adapt to their own situation.

The group's description emphasizes vulnerability and authenticity as prerequisites for the format to work. Members are expected to put themselves on the line — sharing real challenges, not polished success stories. This creates a space where honest conversation can happen, which is rare in business networking contexts where everyone tends to present their best version. The online format via Zoom makes it accessible to people outside Kansas City as well, though the group's roots are in that community.

sections.heading: The Specific Topics
content: The event description lists three specific threads for this session. First, why successful leaders often become prisoners of their own success — the idea that past achievement can create blind spots about future potential. Second, the danger of believing today's business defines tomorrow's potential — a direct challenge to the assumption that current success guarantees future relevance. Third, why comfortable assumptions quietly destroy valuation — the financial consequence of thinking too small.

These three threads build on each other. The first identifies the pattern, the second explains why it happens, and the third shows what it costs. For business owners and leaders, this is a conversation about the gap between where you are and where you could be if you stopped treating your current reality as the ceiling. The format invites participants to reflect on their own businesses and bring specific examples to the discussion.

sections.heading: Participation and Access
content: The event is online via Zoom, with the meeting link visible to attendees after registration. Registration is through Meetup, which is free to join. The session runs for one hour, which keeps the commitment minimal while still allowing enough time for substantive discussion. Since it happens on the first Tuesday of every month, this is part of an ongoing series rather than a standalone event.

For someone running a business who wants a regular space to think strategically about growth, this format offers something that most business resources do: peer conversation with real accountability. The monthly cadence means you can bring a challenge one month, work on it, and report back the next. The online format removes geographic barriers, so you do not need to be in Kansas City to participate. If you have been running your business on autopilot and suspect you are leaving value on the table, this is an hour-long check-in that might shift your perspective.

luma-evt-SN7UWBBLgEM1tmn.summaryLead: A $10 Women of Customer Success event in Austin exploring how the Forward Deployed Engineer role is reshaping Customer Success, featuring panel discussions and roundtable conversations with Cloudflare participation.

sections.heading: The Shift Being Examined
content: WoCS Austin X Cloudflare: The Forward Deployed Era + CS's Shift to Revenue takes place Wednesday, September 24, 2026, from 6:30 PM to 9:30 PM in Austin, Texas. The event, priced at $10, addresses a structural change happening across tech organizations: the emergence of the Forward Deployed Engineer role and how it is pulling technical implementation work away from Customer Success Managers.

The core question is what happens to the CSM role when hands-on technical delivery moves to a dedicated function. The event argues that the CSM seat is not disappearing — it is being redefined around a different core skill: owning revenue. This is not a theoretical discussion. The description notes that this shift is happening industry-wide, and the evening is designed for CS professionals who need to understand what it means for their careers.

sections.heading: The Format and What You Get
content: The evening moves from a panel discussion into small-group roundtable conversations. The panel features leaders and practitioners who have lived through this restructuring firsthand, including, if confirmed, a Cloudflare team member in a Forward Deployed Engineer or Solutions seat. Having someone from Cloudflare — a company that has been vocal about its Forward Deployed approach — in the room gives attendees a concrete example of what this role looks like in practice.

The roundtable portion is where the real work happens. Attendees break into small groups to discuss where they personally sit in this shift, what they should hand off, what they should hold onto, and how to build the language and instincts of someone who owns a revenue number. Bites and beverages are provided, keeping the atmosphere social while the content stays substantive. The combination of panel and roundtable means you leave with both big-picture understanding and specific, personal next steps.

sections.heading: Who Should Attend
content: The event targets four groups: CSMs and Account Managers figuring out what stays on their plate, CS leaders and Directors/VPs who already own or are being asked to own a revenue number, RevOps and CS Ops professionals thinking about team design, and anyone in a post-sales role watching their organization create Forward Deployed Engineer or Solutions Consulting seats. That is a broad but coherent audience — everyone in the room is navigating the same structural shift from a different vantage point.

Women of Customer Success is the organizing community, and the event is built for women working in tech and post-sales roles. WoCS operates with over 10 chapters worldwide, and this Austin edition is part of their broader mission to connect, educate, and empower women in post-sales leadership. The community aspect matters here because the shift being discussed is not just technical — it is career-defining, and having a peer group navigating the same transition adds a support layer that a generic tech event would not provide.

sections.heading: Why This Conversation Is Timely
content: The Forward Deployed Engineer role has gained significant traction in recent years, particularly at companies with complex technical products that require hands-on implementation. As these roles proliferate, the boundary between Customer Success and technical delivery is shifting in real time. CSMs who used to own the full post-sales lifecycle — from onboarding through technical setup to ongoing relationship management — are finding that the technical pieces are being peeled off into dedicated functions.

This creates both opportunity and anxiety. Opportunity, because CSMs who can own revenue and drive expansion are more strategically valuable than ever. Anxiety, because the skills that defined a successful CSM — technical knowledge, product expertise, hands-on implementation ability — are being redistributed. The WoCS Austin event addresses both sides of that equation, giving attendees a framework for understanding where the role is heading and what they need to build toward over the next year to stay ahead of the shift.
